blocks.text: AN ACT
blocks.html: AN ACT

blocks.text: To revise section 48 of title 18, United States Code, and for other purposes.
blocks.html: To revise section 48 of title 18, United States Code, and for other purposes.

blocks.text: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,
blocks.html: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

blocks.text: SECTION 1. Short title.
blocks.html: SECTION 1. Short title.

blocks.text: This Act may be cited as the “Preventing Animal Cruelty and Torture Act” or the “PACT Act”.
blocks.html: This Act may be cited as the “Preventing Animal Cruelty and Torture Act” or the “PACT Act”.

blocks.text: SEC. 2. Revision of section 48.
blocks.html: SEC. 2. Revision of section 48.

blocks.text: (a) In general.—Section 48 of title 18, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:
blocks.html: (a) In general.—Section 48 of title 18, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:

blocks.text: “§ 48. Animal crushing
blocks.html: “§ 48. Animal crushing

blocks.text: “(a) Offenses.—
blocks.html: “(a) Offenses.—

blocks.text: “(1) CRUSHING.—It shall be unlawful for any person to purposely engage in animal crushing in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States.
blocks.html: “(1) CRUSHING.—It shall be unlawful for any person to purposely engage in animal crushing in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States.

blocks.text: “(2) CREATION OF ANIMAL CRUSH VIDEOS.—It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly create an animal crush video, if—
blocks.html: “(2) CREATION OF ANIMAL CRUSH VIDEOS.—It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly create an animal crush video, if—

blocks.text: “(A) the person intends or has reason to know that the animal crush video will be distributed in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce; or
blocks.html: “(A) the person intends or has reason to know that the animal crush video will be distributed in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce; or

blocks.text: “(B) the animal crush video is distributed in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce.
blocks.html: “(B) the animal crush video is distributed in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce.

blocks.text: “(3) DISTRIBUTION OF ANIMAL CRUSH VIDEOS.—It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly sell, market, advertise, exchange, or distribute an animal crush video in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce.
blocks.html: “(3) DISTRIBUTION OF ANIMAL CRUSH VIDEOS.—It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly sell, market, advertise, exchange, or distribute an animal crush video in, or using a means or facility of, interstate or foreign commerce.

blocks.text: “(b) Extraterritorial application.—This section applies to the knowing sale, marketing, advertising, exchange, distribution, or creation of an animal crush video outside of the United States, if—
blocks.html: “(b) Extraterritorial application.—This section applies to the knowing sale, marketing, advertising, exchange, distribution, or creation of an animal crush video outside of the United States, if—

blocks.text: “(1) the person engaging in such conduct intends or has reason to know that the animal crush video will be transported into the United States or its territories or possessions; or
blocks.html: “(1) the person engaging in such conduct intends or has reason to know that the animal crush video will be transported into the United States or its territories or possessions; or

blocks.text: “(2) the animal crush video is transported into the United States or its territories or possessions.
blocks.html: “(2) the animal crush video is transported into the United States or its territories or possessions.

blocks.text: “(c) Penalties.—Whoever violates this section shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 7 years, or both.
blocks.html: “(c) Penalties.—Whoever violates this section shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 7 years, or both.

blocks.text: “(d) Exceptions.—
blocks.html: “(d) Exceptions.—

blocks.text: “(1) IN GENERAL.—This section does not apply with regard to any conduct, or a visual depiction of that conduct, that is—
blocks.html: “(1) IN GENERAL.—This section does not apply with regard to any conduct, or a visual depiction of that conduct, that is—

blocks.text: “(A) a customary and normal veterinary, agricultural husbandry, or other animal management practice;
blocks.html: “(A) a customary and normal veterinary, agricultural husbandry, or other animal management practice;

blocks.text: “(B) the slaughter of animals for food;
blocks.html: “(B) the slaughter of animals for food;

blocks.text: “(C) hunting, trapping, fishing, a sporting activity not otherwise prohibited by Federal law, predator control, or pest control;
blocks.html: “(C) hunting, trapping, fishing, a sporting activity not otherwise prohibited by Federal law, predator control, or pest control;

blocks.text: “(D) medical or scientific research;
blocks.html: “(D) medical or scientific research;

blocks.text: “(E) necessary to protect the life or property of a person; or
blocks.html: “(E) necessary to protect the life or property of a person; or

blocks.text: “(F) performed as part of euthanizing an animal.
blocks.html: “(F) performed as part of euthanizing an animal.

blocks.text: “(2) GOOD-FAITH DISTRIBUTION.—This section does not apply to the good-faith distribution of an animal crush video to—
blocks.html: “(2) GOOD-FAITH DISTRIBUTION.—This section does not apply to the good-faith distribution of an animal crush video to—

blocks.text: “(A) a law enforcement agency; or
blocks.html: “(A) a law enforcement agency; or

blocks.text: “(B) a third party for the sole purpose of analysis to determine if referral to a law enforcement agency is appropriate.
blocks.html: “(B) a third party for the sole purpose of analysis to determine if referral to a law enforcement agency is appropriate.

blocks.text: “(3) UNINTENTIONAL CONDUCT.—This section does not apply to unintentional conduct that injures or kills an animal.
blocks.html: “(3) UNINTENTIONAL CONDUCT.—This section does not apply to unintentional conduct that injures or kills an animal.

blocks.text: “(4) CONSISTENCY WITH RFRA.—This section shall be enforced in a manner that is consistent with section 3 of the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 (42 U.S.C. 2000bb–1).
blocks.html: “(4) CONSISTENCY WITH RFRA.—This section shall be enforced in a manner that is consistent with section 3 of the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 (42 U.S.C. 2000bb–1).

blocks.text: “(e) No preemption.—Nothing in this section shall be construed to preempt the law of any State or local subdivision thereof to protect animals.
blocks.html: “(e) No preemption.—Nothing in this section shall be construed to preempt the law of any State or local subdivision thereof to protect animals.

blocks.text: “(f) Definitions.—In this section—
blocks.html: “(f) Definitions.—In this section—

blocks.text: “(1) the term ‘animal crushing’ means actual conduct in which one or more living non-human mammals, birds, reptiles, or amphibians is purposely crushed, burned, drowned, suffocated, impaled, or otherwise subjected to serious bodily injury (as defined in section 1365 and including conduct that, if committed against a person and in the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, would violate section 2241 or 2242);
blocks.html: “(1) the term ‘animal crushing’ means actual conduct in which one or more living non-human mammals, birds, reptiles, or amphibians is purposely crushed, burned, drowned, suffocated, impaled, or otherwise subjected to serious bodily injury (as defined in section 1365 and including conduct that, if committed against a person and in the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, would violate section 2241 or 2242);

blocks.text: “(2) the term ‘animal crush video’ means any photograph, motion-picture film, video or digital recording, or electronic image that—
blocks.html: “(2) the term ‘animal crush video’ means any photograph, motion-picture film, video or digital recording, or electronic image that—

blocks.text: “(A) depicts animal crushing; and
blocks.html: “(A) depicts animal crushing; and

blocks.text: “(B) is obscene; and
blocks.html: “(B) is obscene; and

blocks.text: “(3) the term ‘euthanizing an animal’ means the humane destruction of an animal accomplished by a method that—
blocks.html: “(3) the term ‘euthanizing an animal’ means the humane destruction of an animal accomplished by a method that—

blocks.text: “(A) produces rapid unconsciousness and subsequent death without evidence of pain or distress; or
blocks.html: “(A) produces rapid unconsciousness and subsequent death without evidence of pain or distress; or

blocks.text: “(B) uses anesthesia produced by an agent that causes painless loss of consciousness and subsequent death.”.
blocks.html: “(B) uses anesthesia produced by an agent that causes painless loss of consciousness and subsequent death.”.

blocks.text: (b) Technical and conforming amendment.—The table of sections for chapter 3 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking the item relating to section 48 and inserting the following:
blocks.html: (b) Technical and conforming amendment.—The table of sections for chapter 3 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking the item relating to section 48 and inserting the following:

blocks.text: “48. Animal crushing.”.
blocks.html: “48. Animal crushing.”.

blocks.text: SEC. 3. Determination of Budgetary Effects.
blocks.html: SEC. 3. Determination of Budgetary Effects.

blocks.text: The budgetary effects of this Act, and the amendments made by this Act, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage.
